message.reasoning_content:
We need to determine charges. Facts: a public official (尹某) a director-level staff in land resources bureau, accepted bribes (cash, shopping cards, etc.) from a company representative in exchange for favorable treatment in land project bidding and contracting. This is classic bribery (受贿) for a public official. Also possibly "单位受贿" vs "受贿". The list includes both "受贿" and "单位受贿". "受贿" is for individuals (non-state staff? Actually "受贿" is for state functionaries). "单位受贿" is for units (organizations) receiving bribes. Here the individual accepted bribes. So charge: 受贿. Also maybe "滥用职权" because he used his position to benefit others? The facts show he used his position to give favor, but the primary crime is bribery. The list includes "滥用职权" as a separate charge for officials abusing power for personal benefit. In many cases, they charge both "受贿" and "滥用职权". In examples: earlier case with姜1某 had both "受贿;滥用职权". That case involved both receiving bribes and abusing authority. Here, the official accepted bribes and used his position to benefit the briber. That is both "受贿" and "滥用职权". The question: Should we include both? The description: "利用职务之便，为他人谋取利益，非法收受他人现金计13.9万元据为己有". That's bribery. Also "利用职务之便" indicates abuse of power. In many Chinese criminal law, "受贿" is the crime; "滥用职权" is separate if the official also abused authority for personal gain beyond bribery. The facts show he gave favorable treatment in project bidding and contracting. That is abuse of power. So likely both charges.

Thus answer: [罪名]受贿;滥用职权<eoa>
